Research position overview

The project combines large language models with comparative bacterial genomics to investigate pathogen emergence from animal hosts. It aims to identify interpretable molecular signatures associated with host switching.

Official project title: How pathogens emerge: integrating large language models with comparative genomics to uncover the zoonotic potential of bacteria

Supervisor: Dr Michiel Vos, Department of Public Health and Sport Sciences, University of Exeter

Funding and duration

ComponentDetails
TuitionFull tuition, including the international fee difference covered by partner universities
MaintenanceGBP 21,805/year (2026/27 reference; updated annually)
Research supportUp to GBP 5,000/year; award conditions apply
Duration4 years full-time; part-time availability depends on the project

Eligibility and Requirements

A relevant first or upper-second-class degree, or overseas equivalent. Applicants with a lower-second-class degree also need a Master’s. Exeter specifies IELTS 6.5 or an accepted equivalent; check component scores and waiver conditions. International awards are limited to up to 30% of the partnership cohort.

Application dates

ComponentDetails
Application deadline21 October 2026, 17:00 BST (21:00 Pakistan)
Funding start1 October 2027
Exeter academic term20 September 2027; confirm admission arrangements

How to Apply

  1. Read the project description and discuss suitability with its supervisor.
  2. Submit one GW4 BioMed application, selecting up to two projects.
  3. If awarded funding, complete the host university’s admission process.

These projects compete for up to 18 studentships across the partnership; each advert is not a guaranteed funded place. Visa, IHS and relocation costs are excluded. Early closure is possible.

About University of Exeter

The University of Exeter offers postgraduate research across health, life sciences, environmental science and other disciplines. It is a partner in GW4 BioMed alongside Bath, Bristol and Cardiff. Exeter-hosted projects give doctoral researchers access to university supervision and training across the partnership.
